title: Runtime deployment authorization catalog and auto-rollback checks
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: We lack a single, verifiable catalog of deployment entitlements and a standardized evidence bundle for production model rollouts. That creates friction for canaries, A/B tests, and shadow deployments when teams need rapid approvals or when on-call must diagnose why a rollback occurred. Goal: Define an explicit authorization catalog (who can start which kind of rollout), an evidence bundle that is attached to rollout events, and a machine-readable schema for audit logs that enables automated compliance queries and forensic review. Also embed deterministic auto-rollback triggers that tie to the same evidence/logs so rollbacks are auditable and reversible.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A written RBAC catalog mapping roles to allowed rollout actions (canary start, increase traffic, enable shadowing, promote to stable) published in Confluence and linked from the Console.
2) An evidence bundle schema for every rollout event containing: requester identity, approvals, model artifacts (hash), config snapshot, monitored metric baselines, and links to evaluation results.
3) Console prompts and API enforcement for required sign-offs before non-trivial rollouts (>=10% traffic or model change >rho threshold).
4) Auto-rollback policy template implemented for canaries that will roll back if defined metric breaches persist for the configured window.
5) Audit log entries for all rollout state transitions with the defined schema; logs queryable by security and SRE.
6) End-to-end test and a staged rollout of the workflow for one internal model by the release date.
proposal_summary: High level: implement a compact authorization catalog (JSON/YAML) that the Console and API consults at rollout time. Add a required_signoffs flow configurable per project and per deployment class (hosted/dedicated/private). Each rollout creates an evidence bundle (stored in the metadata store and referenced from audit logs). Auto-rollback rules attach to the rollout config, with a default policy template we recommend. RBAC enforcement will be implemented as a combination of Console UI gating and server-side checks in the control plane. We will ship a small CLI and API contract so infra and partner teams can automate approvals (eg. CI/CD).
rbac_matrix:
Role -> Allowed actions:
- Viewer: read rollout metadata and audit logs.
- Operator: start canary up to 5% traffic; view metrics.
- Release Engineer: start canary up to 25%, promote to stable with 2 sign-offs.
- Team Lead: can approve promotions and emergency rollbacks.
- Security Officer: can require additional sign-offs for private deployments and view evidence bundles.
Enforcement: console checks + server-side policy evaluator; fallback: manual ticketing for exceptions.
audit_log_schema: Fields to record for each rollout event: timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_role, action (create|increase|promote|rollback|shadow_on|shadow_off), model_name, model_version_hash, config_snapshot_url, evidence_bundle_url, required_signoffs[], approvals[], metrics_baseline_snapshot_url, trigger_metrics[], auto_rollback_policy_id, reason (free-text), request_id, trace_id. Logs should be immutable and stored with retention policy configurable per org.
required_signoffs:
Default templates:
- Safe canary (<5% or non-config-change): Operator + Team Lead (1 sign-off).
- Risky canary (>=5% or model change flagged by eval delta): Release Engineer + Team Lead + Security Officer (3 sign-offs).
- Private/on-prem rollout: Release Engineer + Security Officer + Compliance Lead.
Overrides allowed via delegated entitlements with expiration and audit trail. All signoffs must include: approver id, approval time, and short rationale.
rollout_plan:
Phased plan for initial implementation:
1) Week 0-2: finalize RBAC catalog and evidence schema; design Console UI flows (mockups).
2) Week 3-5: implement server-side policy evaluator and evidence bundle storage; basic Console gating.
3) Week 6: enable auto-rollback engine with two sample policies; integrate with metrics pipeline.
4) Week 7: internal dogfood rollout for 'internal-chat' model with canary -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% promotion using new flow.
5) Week 8: iterate on feedback, add queryable audit dashboard, ship docs and run training session for SRE and Release teams.
rollback_criteria:
Auto-rollback template (default):
- Primary metric breach: latency P95 increases >40% vs baseline for 3 consecutive 1-min windows.
- Error rate: 5xx rate >1% absolute and >2x baseline for 5m sustained.
- Quality regression: eval delta >0.03 (task-specific metric) persisted across 2 evaluation batches.
- Composite rule: any two of above within 10 minutes triggers rollback.
Manual rollback reasons must be recorded in evidence bundle and require Team Lead approval for promotion attempts later.
monitoring_metrics: Metrics to be attached to the rollout event: request_per_second, latency_p50_p95_p99, 5xx_rate, prompt_token_cost, throughput, model_confidence_delta (task-defined), user-facing metric approximations (CTR/engagement if applicable). Dashboard: per-rollout time series with canary vs baseline overlays and an alert channel integration for auto-rollback notifications.
dependencies: PM-25640 (end-to-end change control for model rollouts)
notes: Trade-offs: strong gating slows fast iterations for smaller teams — we will provide delegated short-lived entitlements and a 'fast-track' for low-risk infra-only changes. Evidence bundles increase metadata storage costs; we're limiting persisted artifacts to references (signed hashes) with optional full snapshot retention for Compliance customers. For private deployments we'll offer an on-prem evidence store connector.
